Mouse Ring Rules

A cat and a mouse on a circle of points. The mouse runs only along the circle, the cat may also take the straight lines across. Can the cat catch the mouse before its steps run out?

The rules

The board
The points lie on a circle; each point is joined to its two neighbours. A few dashed lines cross the circle. Easy has 8 points, Medium 10 and Hard 12. Cat and mouse start at random points, at least three points apart.
Moving
The mouse moves first, then the cat, and so on. On each turn the piece goes one step to a neighbouring point; staying put is not allowed. The mouse uses only the circle. The cat uses the circle and the dashed lines. The mouse may not step onto the cat. Tap a marked point to move there.
Caught or away
When the cat steps onto the mouse's point, the mouse is caught and the cat wins. Nobody gets hurt: the game simply ends. The cat has a fixed number of steps, shown above the board. If it has made them all and the mouse is still free, the mouse gets away and wins.
How many steps
The number of steps is worked out for every start. For two players and when you play the cat, the cat has exactly enough steps to catch the mouse – but only if it never wastes one. When you play the mouse against the computer, the cat has one step less, so a careful mouse can get away.
The computer
Against the computer you choose cat or mouse. Easy makes many mistakes, Medium a few, Hard none. The Hint button shows the best step, and Undo takes your last move back.
